title: Sidewalk Surfing Is Born
description: California surfers nail roller skate wheels to wooden planks to 'surf' the sidewalk when waves are flat. The first crude skateboards emerge in beach communities.

title: First Commercial Skateboards
description: Roller Derby releases the first commercially produced skateboard. It's little more than a shaped plank with clay wheels, but it sparks a craze.

title: First Skateboard Competition
description: The first known skateboard contest is held at Pier Avenue Junior School in Hermosa Beach, California. Makaha sponsors the event.

title: First Crash & Ban Wave
description: After a surge of injuries, cities across the US begin banning skateboarding. The first boom goes bust almost overnight. Skateboarding goes underground.

title: Frank Nasworthy Invents Urethane Wheels
description: Frank Nasworthy adapts urethane roller skate wheels for skateboards, creating Cadillac Wheels. This single innovation transforms ride quality and revives the sport.

title: The Zephyr Team (Z-Boys) Emerge
description: The Z-Boys — including Tony Alva, Jay Adams, and Stacy Peralta — revolutionize skateboarding with an aggressive, surf-inspired style born from the empty pools of drought-era Santa Monica.

title: First Skatepark Opens
description: Skateboard City opens in Port Orange, Florida — one of the first purpose-built skateparks. Hundreds more follow across the US and beyond.

title: Alan Gelfand Invents the Ollie
description: Alan 'Ollie' Gelfand invents the no-hands aerial on vert. The ollie will become the foundational trick of all modern skateboarding.

title: Thrasher Magazine Founded
description: Thrasher launches, becoming the voice of hardcore skate culture. Its DIY punk ethos defines an entire generation of skaters.

title: Second Crash
description: Insurance costs shut down nearly every skatepark in America. Skateboarding's second bust drives riders back to the streets and backyard ramps.

title: Bones Brigade Formed
description: Stacy Peralta assembles the Bones Brigade for Powell-Peralta: Tony Hawk, Steve Caballero, Lance Mountain, Tommy Guerrero, Mike McGill, and Rodney Mullen. Skate history's most legendary team.

title: Rodney Mullen's Flatground Ollie
description: Rodney Mullen adapts the ollie to flat ground, opening an infinite universe of street tricks. He goes on to invent the kickflip, heelflip, and dozens more.

title: Transworld Skateboarding Launches
description: Transworld SKATEboarding magazine begins publishing, offering a more photography-driven alternative to Thrasher. Two magazines, two cultures.

title: Powell-Peralta: The Search for Animal Chin
description: The Bones Brigade's full-length skate video becomes a cultural phenomenon and establishes the skate video as an art form.

title: Street League Culture Takes Hold
description: Street skating fully eclipses vert. Handrails, stairs, ledges, and gaps become the new terrain. Technical tricks rule.

title: First X Games
description: ESPN launches the Extreme Games (later X Games) in Rhode Island. Skateboarding reaches mainstream TV audiences for the first time.

title: Tony Hawk Lands the 900
description: At the 1999 X Games, Tony Hawk lands the first-ever 900 (2.5 aerial rotations) on live TV. It becomes one of the most iconic moments in sports history.

title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater Released
description: Activision releases THPS for PlayStation. The game introduces millions to skate culture, trick names, and punk/hip-hop soundtracks. A generation of skaters is born.

title: Girl/Chocolate & Fully Flared Era
description: The early 2000s see skate video production values skyrocket. Girl, Chocolate, and Lakai push filmmaking boundaries.

title: YouTube & the Democratization of Skate Media
description: YouTube launches (2005) and skaters begin uploading clips directly. The gatekeepers of skate media — magazines, video distributors — start losing their monopoly.

title: Street League Skateboarding (SLS) Founded
description: Rob Dyrdek founds SLS, bringing standardized judging and big prize purses to professional street skateboarding. The contest circuit goes pro.

title: Instagram Transforms Skate Culture
description: Short-form video on Instagram changes how tricks are shared. The 15-second clip replaces the full-length video part for many pros.

title: Skateboarding Added to Olympics
description: The IOC announces skateboarding will debut at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held 2021). The decision is both celebrated and controversial within skate culture.

title: Olympic Debut in Tokyo
description: Skateboarding debuts at the Tokyo Olympics with Street and Park disciplines. Yuto Horigome wins the first-ever Olympic skateboarding gold. Teenagers dominate the women's events.

title: Women's Skateboarding Boom
description: Olympic exposure drives massive growth in women's skateboarding. More women and girls pick up boards than ever before. Brands create dedicated women's lines.

title: Paris 2024 Olympics
description: Skateboarding returns to the Olympics in Paris. The La Concorde venue provides a stunning backdrop. Japan and Australia dominate the medal count.

title: AI & Tech Enter Skating
description: AI-powered trick recognition, community apps, and digital tools for skaters emerge. The intersection of tech and skate culture creates new possibilities.
